title: The science fair plan
text:
Setting: Yuki and Citra are in the school library. They are choosing a project for the science fair.

Yuki: I have an excellent idea. Let's build a volcano with baking soda and vinegar. Everybody loves volcanoes.

Citra: Everybody also built one last year. Mrs Putri said she saw forty of them.

Yuki: Forty? That is a lot. But a volcano is the most exciting project anyway.

Citra: Exciting for who? I would like to try something new. What about a solar oven? You line a pizza box with foil, cover the opening with clear plastic, and the sun heats the inside.

Yuki: Does that really work?

Citra: My cousin made one in Surabaya. He used it to melt chocolate on a sunny afternoon.

Yuki: But what if it is cloudy on the day of the fair?

Citra: The fair is indoors, so we will test the oven in the playground on Tuesday. We can measure the temperature every ten minutes with a thermometer and show our results on a chart.

Yuki: That is more work than a volcano.

Citra: It is more work, but I think the judges will like it. They will see real measurements, not just a messy fizz.

Yuki: Hmm. I am still not sure a solar oven is more fun than a volcano. But I do like the idea of a chart. Let's try it, and if it goes wrong, we will build the volcano instead.

Citra: Deal. I will ask Mrs Putri for a thermometer.

Yuki: And I will bring the pizza box. My family orders pizza every Friday, so we will have one by then.
